Direction name (internal art direction, MUST NOT appear in image): COILED WYRM / VIOLET SLATE. Design a materially different, COMPACT, tall-reading layout. Palette: deep muted aubergine slate #282331 for the UI, dark violet leather #352E44, warm silver-white readable type, moon-white dragon, icy turquoise edge light, and small polished violet mineral accents. The top of the app begins within 30px of the top of the board's upper UI portion. Do not place another generic freestanding dragon portrait in the background. No 3D game engine gloss.

Application layout: low-height horizontal header with a character name and three functional icon controls; compact narrow left navigation, with a comfortably styled LEFT settings flyout shown open alongside it. The visible reading pane fills the remaining right area with high-contrast warm-white paragraphs directly on the violet slate surface, thin dividers between messages, speaker names and claw-ring avatars, no large light rectangular paper cards. Show two longer narrative messages with four modest lines each and one short reply, so the page is visibly a reading instrument. Body text equivalent 20px. Outer empty margins very small. A narrow bottom composer is part of the frame and has a silver claw-rimmed send seal. Menus feature shaped tabs made of layered overlapping scales, soft inset charcoal-violet fields, a horizontal page-width slider with a moonstone thumb, elegant and chunky checkbox states. Labels are functional and readable, never decorative.

Important ornament hierarchy: actual circular avatars are held by THREE CLEAR ANATOMICAL DRAGON TALONS gripping the outer metal rim, with visible knuckles and pointed ends, not feather wreaths. Raised bone-silver cornerwork suggests dragon wings, but keeps many calm undecorated stretches for breathing room. The bottom 20% strip shows five large unlabelled matching closeups: empty-center claw avatar frame, claw gripping vertical frame, a horn/wing corner, scale-tab/slider, curled tail at composer edge. This strip is part of this one concept board, not another UI option. No banner titles, taglines, captions or Latin anywhere. Cleanly rendered painterly comic assets with strong facets and material shading. One coherent finished board only.

Direction name: SILVER DRAGON ON THE OBSIDIAN CODEX. A calm but striking dark reading instrument. The reading plane is deep midnight indigo enamel (#182232) with warm frost-white type, occasional mist-lavender emphasis and thin worked-silver edge accents. No pale green sheets. The dragon leans in from the upper LEFT and lays one broad hand over the top-left corner; the neck arches behind the title line and one hooked claw crosses in front of the silver page rim. Keep the face fully visible and expressive in the top-left art margin, not cropped into a slice. Most of the screen remains readable content, not decorative sky. The left rail consists of compact engraved silver toggles on dark leather; a ~300px left settings flyout fits beside it without stealing the entire screen. Settings use restrained inset navy wells, a moonstone slider thumb and crisp selected states. Long-form chat reads as a continuous bound codex with elegant paragraph and speaker hierarchy, very little boxing. Lower composer is a shallow inset writing ledge with a silver nib-shaped send medallion. Bottom ornament strip has the claw-over-rim closeup, dark silver frame corner and matching elegant menu components; these are all from THIS exact design. Strong hierarchy, intentional spacing, clear depth from occlusion. Produce one finished concept board only.

Direction name: MOON-IVORY DRAGON SCRIPTORIUM. A distinctly LIGHT reading design, like a beautifully illustrated enchanted manuscript crafted from ivory, pale lilac vellum, and matte worked silver. Palette: moon-ivory #ECECF4, light periwinkle shadows #C9CBE0, aubergine ink #302940, iridescent small blue-violet cabochons, no gold and no green. A wide open ivory reading surface occupies the center and right with book-leaf edge depth visible only along the perimeter; inside use clean ink typography and tasteful illuminated speaker initials, fine purple-gray rules and tiny margin emblems instead of floating rectangular message cards. Very little exterior blank space, content and frame fill the screen.

The silver dragon curls from BEHIND the UPPER RIGHT corner of the open manuscript, its neck and bright expressive head leaning over the reading-frame edge; a large near hand hooks over the top rim, the other small claw clasps the outer right rim. Show real contact with the bound edge and a small hand-drawn cast shadow, so it rests on the book rather than being a wallpaper. Keep the face above the text flow and all claws off the paragraphs. Its leftward wing is a pale lilac canopy behind the upper border, not an oversized hero billboard.

The far-left navigation is a slim engraved book-spine with bold lavender tab marks. A LEFT SETTINGS LEAF is open beside it: warm ivory surface, clear aubergine headings, larger differentiated inset controls, horizontal pill dropdowns, silver/blue gem slider thumb, tidy round checkboxes, small indigo section markers, and a comfortable two-column pair of settings where appropriate. Refine the left flyout into a usable crafted editorial form, not a dark green block or endless outlines. Conversation uses two speakers and realistic paragraph rhythm, the bottom composer is a shallow lavender writing strip with an embossed dragon-seal send button.

The bottom design-element strip is a studio arrangement on pale paper: a claw gripping the raised ivory book binding, an embossed silver-and-lilac corner, a delicate dragon seal, a ribbon tab and a native width-slider concept. These are design details for this SAME screen, not another alternative. Maintain comic hand drawing and angular cel-shaded dragon anatomy; luxurious but crisp and usable. One completed concept board only.
